question.problem: Given a rectangular solid, find the differential $\text{d}S$ for the surface area $S$ of the rectangular solid if the base is a square with the side of $a=3$ and the height is $h=7.$
question.worked_solution:
The surface area of the given rectangular solid is $S=2{a}^{2}+4ah.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}S(a,h) & =(\frac{∂S}{∂a})\,\text{d}a+(\frac{∂S}{∂h})\,\text{d}h \\  & =(4a+4h)\,\text{d}a+4a\,\text{d}h\end{aligned}
$$

For $a=3$ and $h=7,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}S(3,7) & =(4\cdot 3+4\cdot 7)\,\text{d}a+4\cdot 3\,\text{d}h \\  & =40\,\text{d}a+12\,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$
